hook: Hot sleeper? Summer is coming.
fact: Keeps your bed at the temperature you choose

hook: What does 1.5 ATA actually mean?
fact: At 1.5 ATA, the air around you is at 50% more pressure than at sea level

hook: Your legs have a second heart.
fact: Your calf muscles squeeze to push blood back up towards your heart

hook: Why 1070nm light?
fact: Near-infrared light at 1070nm travels deeper than the red light most devices use

hook: Ever trained your breathing muscles?
fact: Your diaphragm is a muscle, and like any muscle it responds to resistance training

hook: You won't feel it. That's the point.
fact: PEMF sends gentle electromagnetic pulses into the area a device sits on

hook: Tight spots holding you back?
fact: Percussive therapy delivers rapid, targeted pulses deep into muscle

hook: Why cool beats icy.
fact: These PCM packs freeze at around 15°C, not 0°C like ice

hook: Light, but make it wearable.
fact: Photobiomodulation is the science of how light interacts with your cells

hook: Adding hyperbaric to your clinic?
fact: A rigid hard shell means no inflating and no sagging between clients

hook: Built for clinics.
fact: High-frequency vibration works soft tissue without the pounding of a massage gun

hook: Can standing still train your bones?
fact: Bone is living tissue that responds to mechanical signals

hook: Salon-style light therapy, at home.
fact: LED masks use red light and near-infrared light, each a different wavelength

hook: Too hot for you, too cold for them?
fact: Water holds about 4x more heat than the same weight of air

hook: How roomy is a 36 inch chamber?
fact: 36 inches is about 91 cm, close to the height of a kitchen bench

hook: Light, without the heat.
fact: LEDs turn far more of their energy into light than old-style bulbs, so they run cool

hook: 5 metres underwater. In your living room.
fact: 1.5 ATA is about the pressure you'd feel 5 metres under the sea

hook: Light your eyes can't see.
fact: Human eyes see light from about 400 to 700nm; 1070nm sits well beyond red

hook: No hoses. No pump box.
fact: Most compression boots run off a separate pump box, connected by air hoses

hook: It's not just speed. It's stroke.
fact: Amplitude is how far a massage gun's head travels with every pulse

hook: Who looks after the therapist's hands?
fact: Hands-on soft tissue work puts repeated load through a therapist's hands and wrists

hook: Why sweat stops working on muggy days.
fact: Sweat only cools you when it evaporates; in humid air it drips instead

hook: Why hot nights feel so restless.
fact: Your core body temperature naturally dips as you drift off to sleep

hook: Why a helmet, not a panel?
fact: Light spreads out as it travels, so it gets weaker the further it has to go

hook: About 20,000 breaths a day.
fact: You take roughly 20,000 breaths a day, and your diaphragm powers most of them

hook: What does the 30 in Quest30 mean?
fact: 30 inches is about 76 cm, the chamber's width

hook: Your skeleton is always being rebuilt.
fact: Bone is constantly renewed; your skeleton is largely replaced about every 10 years

hook: What makes a compass point north?
fact: Earth has a magnetic field; it's what turns a compass needle north

hook: Why do your ears pop on a plane?
fact: Ears pop when the air pressure around you changes, like on a plane's descent

hook: Why are sunsets red?
fact: Red light has longer wavelengths, so it scatters less and travels further through the air

hook: Why are pressure tanks always round?
fact: Curved walls spread pressure evenly, so there are no weak corners

hook: What does Hz actually mean?
fact: One hertz means once per second; Australian mains power alternates at 50 Hz

hook: Why squeeze toothpaste from the bottom?
fact: Squeezing in order from one end moves everything the same way; squeezing the middle pushes both ways

hook: Why do builders use a hammer drill?
fact: A hammer drill adds rapid blows to the spin, so rhythm does the work rather than pushing harder
